description: Which Georgia public school attendance zones (elementary, middle, high) contain a place, or (attendance_rules=true) how attendance zones work in Georgia. Give exactly one of: lat + lon; an address (geocoded by the U.S. Census Geocoder); a 2020 census tract_geoid (returns every zone covering the tract with the share of its 2020 population in each, or, when none does, a coverage_reason saying why); or attendance_rules=true with no place. Optional grade (pk, k, 01-12) and year. Returns the district, the zoned schools with labels and provenance (method, accuracy_class, positional_rmse_m, boundary_vintage, currency_status, currency_note, source_url), a level_status per school level, a coverage_status (zoned, gap — some level has no zone there — one_school_per_grade, not_available — the district publishes no zones at some level — with the reason, not_zoned — no zone assigns the grade asked, i.e. pre-K), a currency_warning when a zone's source predates an adopted change that could not be applied (it quotes what changed, by level), an overlap_warning when two schools' zones cover the point for the same grades (it names them, by level), the point's tract and county, and a geojson_url per zone — never the polygons themselves. Zones are reconstructed from published sources of varying currency and are NOT an official enrollment determination: always tell the user to confirm with the district. The zoned school is the default assignment (the result's assignment_note says so). attendance_rules=true returns instead who draws zones and the main ways a student attends a public school other than the zoned one, with the statute or rule behind each: use it when a user asks how zones work or whether a child must attend the zoned school. A dated summary, not legal advice; lang="es" gives it in Spanish.
name: lookup_school_zone
